hero.title: M3A Team
hero.subtitle: Minsait Multi-Agent AI Framework — specialized agents orchestrated inside VS Code, with GitHub Copilot

about.heading: What is M3A Team?
about.p1: M3A Team (Multi-Agent AI Architecture) is an enterprise-grade, reusable multi-agent AI ecosystem designed for any Minsait project — new or existing, any stack, any domain.
about.p2: It provides a team of 12 specialized AI agents, each with a distinct persona inspired by historical and intellectual figures. Agents collaborate on quality gates, enforce architectural decisions, and produce executive-grade documentation — all within VS Code using GitHub Copilot Agent mode.
about.p3: No external services, no cloud subscriptions beyond Copilot. Install with one command, activate with /m3a-init, and your entire team gains a structured AI workforce governed by 13 immutable laws.
about.highlight1_desc: No external tools or platforms. Agents run as Copilot agent modes directly in your editor.
about.highlight2_desc: Everything lives in your repository under .github/ — fully version-controlled and reviewable via PR.
about.highlight3_desc: Governance baked into every agent: knowledge-first, no silence in reviews, mandatory consensus, operational honesty.

agents.heading: The Agent Roster
agents.description: 12 specialized agents, each with a distinct persona and area of expertise. Click any card to see full capabilities.

orchestrator.motto: Governs without executing — decisions under pressure with rationality and long-term vision.
capabilities: Routes requests to the correct specialized agent
Manages epic creation and approval flow
Consolidates review verdicts from all agents
Records all project decisions in the knowledge base

analyst.motto: Decompose each problem into parts until nothing remains unexplained.
capabilities: Shallow, intermediate, and deep component analysis
EOL verification and technology lifecycle mapping
Knowledge base construction from codebase scanning

architect.motto: Firmitas, Utilitas, Venustas — good architecture serves purpose, is robust, and survives through time.
capabilities: TO-BE architecture design and migration planning
Epic risk assessment with elevated veto power

pm.motto: Effectiveness is doing the right things. What generates no value does not exist.
capabilities: Epic creation with structured brainstorm process

sm.motto: Good results come from good systems, not heroes.
capabilities: Story creation and decomposition from epics
Definition of Ready / Definition of Done enforcement

dev.motto: Premature optimization is the root of all evil. Code must survive decades.

qa.motto: Only what can be falsified can be validated.
capabilities: Test strategy and planning per story/epic
Acceptance criteria validation and testability review
Definition of Done enforcement at quality gates
Test coverage strategy and gap analysis

security.motto: Without adequate security, systems are solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
capabilities: OWASP Top 10 audit and compliance checking
CVE dependency scanning and remediation plans
Attack surface analysis and threat modeling
VETO power — blocks any unsafe epic or story

devops.motto: Without reliable infrastructure, software does not exist in production.

docs.motto: The challenge is not to create — it is to structure so it can be found.

ux.motto: Good design makes complex things understandable.
capabilities: Design system review and consistency checks
User journey mapping and flow optimization
UI component analysis and improvement proposals

dba.motto: Data shall be accessed by its content, not by its location.
capabilities: Query performance tuning and indexing strategy
ORM evaluation and data access layer review

features.heading: Key Features
features.description: A comprehensive AI-powered engineering workflow — from idea to production.

bootstrap.title: New Product Bootstrap
bootstrap.description: Go from a product idea to your first sprint in a structured, agent-guided process.
steps: Drucker creates the PRD and defines the product vision
Vitruvius designs the TO-BE architecture with C4 diagrams
Atlas generates DevContainers and CI/CD scaffolding
Descartes scans the landscape and builds the knowledge base
Deming plans Sprint 1 with stories and acceptance criteria

quality_gates.title: Quality Gates
quality_gates.story_desc: 5 agents perform a surgical review of every completed story. QA, Security, and Developer hold veto power — one rejection blocks the story.
quality_gates.epic_desc: Up to 9 agents perform a systemic review of the entire epic. Architect and DBA gain elevated veto power. No agent may remain silent.
quality_gates.epic_agents: QA · Security · Developer · Architect · Docs · PM + DBA · DevOps · UX

knowledge.title: Knowledge-Driven
knowledge.description: Every decision, convention, and architectural choice is recorded in a structured knowledge base that grows with your project.
points: Descartes builds the knowledge base from deep codebase scans
Marcus Aurelius records all decisions in the decisions log
Borges curates and structures documentation for discoverability
All agents read knowledge before acting — Law 1: Knowledge First

multistack.title: Multi-Stack Support
multistack.description: Works on any technology stack. MMA auto-detects your project's languages, frameworks, and tools — then adapts all 12 agents accordingly.
multistack.stacks: Java · .NET · Python · Node.js · Go · Angular · React · Vue · and more

executive_docs.title: Executive Documentation
executive_docs.description: Borges translates technical analysis into executive-grade reports with Minsait branding.
points: Minsait-branded HTML portals with ForFutureSans typography
Sprint reports, epic summaries, risk registers

security_first.title: Security First
security_first.description: Hobbes has absolute VETO power — no unsafe epic or story passes review. Security is not an afterthought, it's enforced at every gate.
points: OWASP Top 10 audit on every review
CVE dependency scanning with remediation plans
System hardening and attack surface analysis
Security baseline enforcement across all stacks

existing_project.title: Existing Projects & Modernization
existing_project.description: Start from an existing codebase — legacy system, monolith, or partial refactoring. MMA maps the AS-IS state, identifies technical debt, and builds a structured modernization roadmap.
steps: Descartes runs AS-IS analysis: stack scan, CVEs, module decomposition
Knowledge base built from codebase, docs, and architecture artifacts
Vitruvius designs the TO-BE architecture with migration gap analysis
Hobbes audits security posture and CVE exposure
Drucker creates a modernization roadmap with prioritized epics

laws.heading: 13 Immutable Laws
laws.description: Governance baked into every agent. Absolute, inviolable, applied at every interaction.

items.name: Knowledge First
items.desc: Every agent reads the knowledge base before any action. New knowledge physically updates the files — never stays in chat only.

items.name: Minimal Chat
items.desc: Only status formats in chat: ✅ file, ⚠️ warning, ❌ blocked. No narration, no reasoning, no content duplication.

items.name: Anti-Duplicate
items.desc: Before creating anything, check the backlog for similar epics, stories, and analyses already done.

items.name: Continuous Learning
items.desc: Every new relevant knowledge about the project physically updates the knowledge base — never gets lost.

items.name: War Room = Human Only
items.desc: No agent triggers a War Room automatically. Agents can only suggest it to the human with clear justification.

items.name: No Silence in Review
items.desc: Every agent evaluates every epic through their specialized lens. Silence requires explicit documented justification.

items.name: Mandatory Consensus
items.desc: Disagreements between agents must be resolved with evidence exchange. Unresolved after 2 rounds → escalate to human.

items.name: Sprint-by-Sprint
items.desc: Never detail beyond Sprint N+1. Each sprint is refined based on actual results of the previous sprint.

items.name: Multi-Agent Approval
items.desc: No epic advances from draft to approved with any agent blocked (❌). All 12 agents must review and respond.

items.name: Two Output Layers
items.desc: Layer 1: operational/technical (internal). Layer 2: executive (for management). Docs agent translates between them.

items.name: Agent Versioning
items.desc: Every agent update increments semantic version and adds a changelog entry. Full traceability is mandatory.

items.name: Build Always Passes
items.desc: No story is done without evidence of a passing build. Build broken = story returns to in-progress.

items.name: Operational Honesty
items.desc: An agent that skipped a mandatory step must actively declare it. Silence about a deviation equals a false declaration.

install.heading: Install M3A Team
install.description: One command installs all 12 agents into any VS Code project with GitHub Copilot.
install.prereq_desc: Make sure you have all three before running the install script.
install.prereq_vscode: VS Code with GitHub Copilot extension
install.step1_desc: Execute from your project root (where .git/ lives)
install.step2_desc: Personalizes config and activates all 12 agents for your project
install.step2_callout: Required before any other command. /m3a-init configures agents with your project stack, team, and context. Without it, agents operate without project knowledge.
install.step3_desc: Recommended for existing projects — deep codebase scan that powers all agent analysis
install.step4_desc: All /m3a-* commands are now available in Copilot Chat
